correctness.rationale: Reduction of the universal integral binary-cubic discriminant modulo 3 yields Δ=b²c²−ac³−b³d, with four derivatives exactly −c³, −bc², −b²c, −b³. Therefore the projective intrinsic Jacobian ideal is (b,c)^3; the graded pieces of its third infinitesimal line neighborhood have Hilbert polynomial (n+1)+2n+3(n−1)=6n−2. The repeated-linear-factor morphism from P¹×P¹ is proper, finite, birational, radicial and induces cubic Frobenius over L. On chart a≠0, the finite normal free-module lattice R=k[b,d]⊕k[b,d](bt)⊕k[b,d](b²t²)⊂k[b,d]⟨1,t,t²⟩ with t³+bt²=d gives conductor b²S=(b,c)^2; the symmetric chart d≠0 covers the rest of the singular line, and the complement is normal, so the global conductor is I_L². Finite-field Frobenius bijectivity gives #(D(F_q))=(q+1)²; zeta formula follows, while standard quartic hypersurface and Künneth cohomology give H²(O_D)=k versus H²(O_P1×P1)=0. Independent characteristic-3 symbolic derivative check confirms the Jacobian; source verification code includes finite GF(3)/GF(9) projective enumeration but not proof of all fields.
